shouldFix.title: The after-cells drop the applied-state marker and the full artifact digest that the register's own candidate-recording form uses, on the two rows that are hard blockers for preview analyze
shouldFix.finding: File 08 already has a settled form for recording an accepted design-contract candidate on a row that stays OPEN, and it is used on both rows where it has arisen. DR-114: '[`doctor-contract.v4.json`](…) `df2e717555616db096e61548458f23b442f7f0e37b2d2461eabc2c33201e94b3` — `CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED`, binds NOTHING — reviewed ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES, 0 blockers ([verdict](…) `d6328807…`)'. DR-105 carries the same construction for permission-truth-tables.v1. The form has three load-bearing parts: a link to the artifact, its full 64-hex digest, and the explicit `CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED`, binds NOTHING marker. D-140's after-cells carry none of the three. They read 'accepted design-contract candidate recorded (D-136; provider-only-output-contract.v3.json `ef2a7416…`)' — filename without a link, digest truncated to eight hex, and no applied-state marker at all. The marker is not a house-style flourish. D-136's own Decision says in terms 'Candidate binds NOTHING', and the whole corpus discipline around candidates — delivery.v4's 'applicationState: NOT APPLIED, binds NOTHING', D-133's rule that a recorded candidate does not make a row eligible in kind — exists to stop a recorded artifact being read as in force. DR-131 and DR-133 are labelled in their own Impact cells as 'Hard blocker for preview analyze'. A reader of the live register after this edit learns that an accepted contract candidate exists for each blocker and that the rows are not SATISFIED, but not that the contracts bind nothing and have not been applied. That is a weaker statement in the authoritative surface than the two precedent rows make, and MF-6 cell content is exactly what this entry is for.
shouldFix.whyNotMustFix: Nothing unlawful follows. The rows stay OPEN, no SATISFIED is added, eligibility in kind is refused in the same cell, and condition-2 arithmetic is untouched. The defect is that the cell under-states the artifacts' status relative to the register's own convention, not that it asserts anything false.

shouldFix.title: Performing H1 and H2 in one act departs from the schedule D-139 pinned, without acknowledging the text it departs from, and couples the two rows' reversibility
shouldFix.finding: D-139's H preamble, in the turn-2 subject that COORD pins at `b5fa22c3…`, reads: 'These may run in any order. Each is its own later D-000 cycle and commit.' D-138 describes its own owed act the same way: 'That MF-6 act — its own D-000 cycle and commit — updates that cell.' D-140 instead states 'Performs D-139 H1 and H2 in one act: the two owed cell updates are the same class.' That is one cycle and one commit for two H nodes. The entry never quotes or engages the 'each is its own' text; a reader of D-140 alone would not know an adopted schedule, three commits old, says otherwise, and the same-class justification is D-140's own reasoning rather than anything D-139 or D-138 supplies. The concrete cost shows up in this entry's own Reversibility: 'Overturn restores the two `no contract exists` clauses' — the two cells can now only be reverted together, whereas D-139's per-node structure and its 'after any dependent H or L act lands' reversibility contemplated them landing and unwinding separately. If one of the two underlying recordings were later disturbed and the other stood, the coupled act is the harder thing to unwind.
shouldFix.counterReadingAcknowledged: A purposive reading is available and may well be what was intended: 'each is its own D-000 cycle and commit' may mean only that no hygiene act rides along on an unrelated decision, and D-140 does satisfy that — it is a dedicated, independently reviewed, separately committed act covering two cells of one class. I am not asserting the merge is unlawful. I am asserting that a departure from a digest-pinned adopted schedule should be visible in the entry that makes it.
shouldFix.whyNotMustFix: No governance step is skipped. Both cells receive the same adversarial review in this cycle, the same prohibitions apply, and the act is committed on its own. The defect is schedule fidelity and reversibility granularity, both repairable in a clause.
shouldFix.repair: Either split into two acts, one per cell, which is what the pinned text most naturally reads as requiring; or keep the single act and add one clause that quotes D-139's 'Each is its own later D-000 cycle and commit', states that a single dedicated D-000 cycle and commit covering two same-class cells satisfies it, and records that the two rows' reversibility is thereby coupled. If the coordinator prefers the merged form as a general rule, that is a change to D-139's H structure and belongs in a D-139 amendment rather than in the act that first departs from it.

advisories.title: The 'after (verbatim)' strings nest backticks inside backtick-delimited quotes, so the exact bytes to write are not unambiguously specified

coordinatorSummary: OBJECT at 0 MUST-FIX, 2 SHOULD-FIX, 2 advisories. Fifteen attacks run, four landed. Custody is clean: subject be41007c at 0444 unmoved at both ends with dispatch and prompt agreeing, HEAD never left ca42347, file 08 at 7585325d and COORD at 801a5f58 with a clean tree. The mechanical core of the entry holds under the sharpest tests. Both before-quotes are byte-exact against the live cells, the locator rule resolves uniquely — one line begins with each row prefix and 'no contract exists' occurs exactly twice in the whole file — the two contract digests are identical to those D-136 and D-138 record and the artifacts still hash to them at 0444, the row-to-artifact mapping is not transposed, the after-strings contain no pipe, and 'accepted design-contract candidate' is D-136's own term rather than an upgrade. The authority chain is real: D-136 names the owed MF-6 on DR-133's clause, D-138 on DR-131's cell, and adopted D-139 lists both under H. What blocks is two things. First, the after-cells drop the form the register itself uses for this exact act. DR-114 and DR-105 both record accepted candidates as a linked artifact, a full 64-hex digest, and the marker `CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED`, binds NOTHING; D-140's cells carry none of the three, giving a bare filename, an eight-hex truncation, and no applied-state marker — this on the two rows file 08 itself labels hard blockers for preview analyze, and against D-136's own words 'Candidate binds NOTHING'. A reader of the live register after this edit would learn a contract candidate exists and the row is not SATISFIED, but not that the contract binds nothing and has not been applied. Second, the entry performs H1 and H2 in one act while D-139's digest-pinned text says 'Each is its own later D-000 cycle and commit' and D-138 describes its owed act the same way; the entry never engages that text, and its own Reversibility consequently couples the two rows so neither cell can be reverted alone. I record the purposive counter-reading — a dedicated, reviewed, separately committed act covering two same-class cells may well satisfy the intent — and my objection is that a departure from a pinned schedule should be visible in the entry making it, not that the merge is unlawful. Both repairs are small: rewrite the two cells in the established candidate form, and either split the act or add one reconciling clause. The advisories are that the 'after (verbatim)' strings nest backticks inside backtick-delimited quotes so the exact bytes are not unambiguously specified, and that the duplicate-heading parenthetical points at f7afe45, which changed no COORD bytes — the duplicate came from 3b84beb, and the operative claim of one live '## D-139' heading measures true at exactly 1.
